model_annotation: Figure 4 is a line plot illustrating the performance of different knowledge editing methods on long-tail biomedical knowledge, measured as accuracy percentage (%) on the y-axis against co-occurrence number groups on the x-axis. The x-axis is categorical, divided into four groups: “<10¹”, “[10¹, 10²)”, “[10², 10³)”, and “≥10³”, representing increasing levels of triple co-occurrence frequency. The y-axis is linear, ranging from 55% to 65%, with major tick marks at 55, 60, and 65. Five distinct lines are plotted, each representing a different editing method: Base (black solid line with circle markers), FT (blue dashed line with square markers), MEMIT (purple dash-dotted line with diamond markers), IKE (red dotted line with triangle markers), and ROME (green solid line with cross markers). All lines show a general upward trend as co-occurrence number increases, indicating improved performance on more frequent knowledge. For example, ROME starts at approximately 56% for the <10¹ group and rises to about 63% for the ≥10³ group. Similarly, Base begins near 55% and ends around 58%. The relative ordering of methods remains fairly consistent across groups, with ROME consistently achieving the highest performance, followed by FT, MEMIT, IKE, and Base. The legend is positioned in the top-left corner of the plot.
